checks: No eclipse at 1 of 67 covered epochs where the 1.32885 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 59458906 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.328846 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse causes a dimming of 0.49%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal has a high detection significance of 973.7 in the box-least-squares search, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise of 14.1 with a centroid offset of 0.4 arcsec from the target position. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it represents a previously unknown system. However, the odd/even eclipse depths show a significant difference (z-score 9.79), indicating that successive eclipses vary in depth - a pattern consistent with a true period that is twice the initially detected value. While pixel-check confirmation and eclipse timing remain unaffected by this anomaly, the alternating eclipse depths represent an open question about the system's true characteristics
